catalog_quote: As a general rule all Konkani words have the accent on the last syllable. 1. I do not reckon as a syllable that which ends in a or u. Hence the accent falls upon the preceding syllable, because the preceding syllable is truly the last full syllable.

audit.action: check whether this is the same language as another entry
audit.recode_to: Re-key the row to goan1235 (dialect mang1376 Karnataka Christian Konkani); then re-settle the stress coding: 'fixed-strict final' cannot stand unqualified against held Madtha 1984 p.17 (initial stress, same lect) and Peterson 2011 (weight-sensitive rightmost, via Ashok & Dutta 2021). Pending Almeida 1989 / Miranda 2003 / Peterson 2011 first-hand, at minimum downgrade to contested (final per Maffei 1882 + LSI 1905 vs initial per Madtha 1984 + Katre 1966) and add Madtha as a 'contra' source; note also that Maffei's own clause 1 makes the rule 'last FULL syllable' (final reduced a/u skipped), which the strict-final rule string does not encode.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Maffei 1882 passage is verbatim at ch. II pp. 7-8 in the held scanned ( lines 1321-1361), addenda p. 397 also present. (2) Deciding source: an 1882 Jesuit pedagogical grammar of Mangalore Christian Konkani, self-hedged ('cannot perceive distinctly whether it is upon the last or upon the penultimate'). It is not the best available description: Almeida 1989 (reference grammar, 338 pp.), Miranda 2003 (Routledge handbook chapter) and Peterson 2011 (Jazyki mira sketch with a stated stress algorithm) exist and are not yet obtained; and a held 1984 linguistic thesis on the identical lect (Madtha, Christian Konkani of South Kanara, p. 17) says the INITIAL syllable is stressed, agreeing with Katre 1966 sec. 25 and disagreeing with Maffei/LSI 1905/Kamath 2004 (final). Ghatage 1963 (downloaded now) is silent. (3) Identity: Glottolog konk1267 is 'Konkan Marathi
audit.second_reader_evidence: Independent re-check of every claim in the assessment, all confirmed at page level. (1) QUOTE: lines 1321-1330 'CHAPTER II. ACCENT.. As a general rule all Konkani words have the accent on the last syllable. 1. I do not reckon as a syllable that which ends in a or u. Hence the accent falls upon the preceding syllable, because the preceding syllable is truly the last full syllable.' followed by page marker '8' and 'Exceptions 1. The cardinal numbers from 11 to 18.. 2. Raja, sade and a few other words have the accent upon the penultimate. 3. Foreign words adopted, chiefly family-names, retain their original accent' -- verbati

sources.quote: 'All mono-syllabic words are stressed at the vowel point. In di-syllabic words stress falls on the second syllable. In tri-syllabic words stress falls on the third syllable.' ... 'When a mono syllabic word takes pratyaya, the stress accent is found to be shifted to the later syllable' (ghar -> gharaak, stress on raa); 'in Konkani stress accent is mistaken for the duration of the vowel'. Kochi (Kerala GSB) Konkani; a spelling-reform essay, not a linguistic description.
